newsitem.title: UK: British find lethal IRA sniper gun.
newsitem.headline: British find lethal IRA sniper gun.

text.p: British forces said on Saturday they had seized a lethal IRA sniper rifle in a security operation seen as a heavy blow to guerrillas on the border between Northern Ireland and the Irish republic.

Security sources said a U.S.- manufactured Barrett "Light Fifty" gun, along with Kalashnikov assault rifle and ammunition, was recovered and seven men arrested near Crossmaglen in County Armagh, known as "bandit country" for its history of anti-British activity.

The men, detained when the search operation began last Thursday, were still being questioned, a police spokesman said. "A number of motor vehicles have also been siezed. The operation is continuing," he added.

It was aimed at capturing weapons used by Irish Republican Army (IRA) snipers, who have killed 11 British soldiers and policemen along the border during the conflict over Britain's rule over Northern Ireland.
"It is obviously a major success for the security forces," said Paul Connolly, security correspondent of the Belfast Telegraph. "Security people will be cock-a-hoop about this one."
Security analysts believe the IRA has only a handful of the Barrett "Light Fifty" guns, but they are among the most formidable weapons in their extensive armoury.

The experts say the guns, which have a range of 2,000 metres (6,500ft) and fire large armour-piercing bullets, have been used along with other high calibre weapons in deadly single-shot attacks on British patrols since 1992.

An IRA sniper killed a British soldier at a security checkpoint in Bessbrook, Country Armagh, in February. A policewoman shot in the back in the centre of Londonderry city last Thursday is still seriously ill, hospital sources say.
Darwin Templeton, a security specialist on the Belfast's Sunday Life newspaper, described the Barrett "Light Fifty" as extremely powerful.

"It is a major coup for the security forces in an area like South Armagh which is an nationalist stronghold. The security forces suspect that there maybe two or three IRA units in the area carrying out these sniper attacks. It is a major success for them to have retrieved this weapon," he said.
A car, specially fitted with armour plating and of a type known to have been used in IRA gun attacks, was also found, security sources said.
